question: How should a Stellar API choose between x402, MPP, and other emerging agent-payment protocols without locking its application to one standard?

golden.answer: Choose by interaction and settlement model, then isolate it behind an adapter covering quote/payment intent, payment evidence, settlement, fulfillment, idempotency, and refunds. x402 V2 and MPP both use HTTP 402 but have different payloads and infrastructure. x402 V2 has extensions and discovery, but its core specification leaves session handling to applications. MPP Charge settles on-chain while Session uses a channel for repeated traffic. AP2 supplies authorization, mandate, and audit semantics that can sit above a rail; ACP is a beta commerce protocol for catalog, cart, checkout, and orders, not Stellar settlement. Cite each protocol's own specification and keep entitlement independent.
keyFacts: The x402 V2 and MPP HTTP-402 protocols differ in payloads, settlement, and infrastructure.
x402 V2 provides extensions and discovery.
MPP uses on-chain Charge settlement and cumulative off-chain Session channel commitments.
AP2/ACP cover above-rail authorization/mandate/audit and beta commerce, respectively.
avoid: x402, MPP, AP2, and ACP are interchangeable names for the same protocol.
MPP always requires one on-chain transaction for every paid response.
Do NOT claim ACP is Stellar settlement.
Do NOT place application-level session handling inside the x402 V2 core specification.
golden.notes: Status-sensitive details are stated as of 2026-08-04; grade later sourced changes leniently and require dated primary evidence.

corroboration.claim: x402 V2 and MPP are distinct HTTP-402 protocols with different payloads, settlement, and infrastructure; x402 V2 has extensions and discovery, while session handling is application-level and outside its core specification.

evidence.note: Out of Scope list includes 'Session handling mechanisms'; defines extensions and '8. Discovery API'.
Stellar MPP uses the paymentauth draft-stellar-charge-00 method with SEP-41 transfers, a different payload than x402.
MPP site lists separate sessions and x402-compatibility updates, so the two remain distinct protocols.

corroboration.claim: MPP Charge settles on-chain, while MPP Session uses cumulative off-chain channel commitments.

evidence.note: 'Each payment is a Soroban SEP-41 transfer settled on-chain individually'; Channel mode signs 'cumulative commitments — no per-payment on-chain transactions'.
'An improved sessions experience' (2026-06-17) for pay-as-you-go billing.

corroboration.claim: AP2 supplies authorization/mandate/audit semantics above a rail; ACP is a beta commerce protocol, not Stellar settlement.

evidence.note: 'Mandates are the core means that AP2 uses to authorize agents'; Checkout and Payment Mandates and receipts serve as evidence.
'The specification is maintained by OpenAI and Stripe and is currently in beta'; latest spec 2026-04-17 covers cart, feed, orders.

corroboration.claim: A protocol adapter covers quote/payment intent, payment evidence, settlement, fulfillment, idempotency, and refunds.

evidence.note: The 2026-04-17 checkout OpenAPI mentions idempotency 46 times; examples include orders/digital-fulfillment.json and orders/refunded-order.json.
Core types PaymentRequirements, PaymentPayload, and SettlementResponse separate payment intent, evidence, and settlement.

corroboration.claim: x402, MPP, AP2, and ACP are interchangeable names for the same protocol.

evidence.note: x402 V2 is its own specification.
ACP is a separate commerce specification.
AP2 is a separate mandate specification.

corroboration.claim: MPP always requires one on-chain transaction for every paid response.

evidence.note: Channel mode makes many off-chain payments with no per-payment on-chain transactions.
